A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide comparable text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–I. V4 adds appendix subsections and removes the NeurIPS checklist; these are identifiable revisions rather than missing evidence.

before.justification: V3 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations in Appendix D and CIFAR-10 classification experiments in Section 8 and Appendix H.

after.justification: V4 retains the original Gaussian-mixture simulations and CIFAR-10 experiments, including their numerical results and uncertainty reporting.

M1.justification: The linear/logistic SD models, losses, pseudo-label rules, and early-stopping and bias-fixing procedures remain unchanged. New Algorithm 1 documents computation within the replica-equation solver already described in Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian-mixture binary classification and CIFAR-10 cat-versus-dog classification using ResNet-18/50 features. The added non-Gaussian validity claim and anisotropy discussion introduce no evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same optimal 0-SD, soft-label and hard-label SD, noiseless-reference, and fixed-bias variants. Newly cited research is not introduced as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Corresponding figure parameters and Appendix G's preprocessing, feature dimensions, subset sampling, noise injection, and hyperparameter-tuning procedures are unchanged. Appendix C.11 expands computational documentation without reporting revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 6 newly reports a preliminary analysis of optimized regularization schedules, finding very large initial regularization followed by zero regularization. This supplies additional support for early stopping; the existing ablations and supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 5 and 9 retain standard errors over 10 trials per point, and Figure 7 retains standard errors over 20 trials. No changed run counts, seed information, or statistical estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The plotted results and image examples are unchanged. V4 adds the qualitative empirical finding in Section 6 that black-box optimization produces regularization schedules starting very large and then switching to zero; no new numerical performance comparison accompanies it.

T1.justification: V4 restores the temperature factor beta_t in Equation (137), adds an implicit-differentiation derivation in Appendix C.11, and states a non-Gaussian extension in the Section 3.1 footnote. The principal replica and phase-transition formulas are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about denoising, limited dark-knowledge benefits, dataset-size dependence, early stopping, bias fixing, and qualitative CIFAR-10 validation.

C2.justification: Section 4 and new Appendix C.10 explicitly acknowledge that a rigorous proof remains open and explain the obstacle posed by temporal correlations. New Appendix I.1 discusses how anisotropy could help or harm SD, while Section 6 clarifies predictive diversity as uncertainty.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.11 documents fixed-point iteration, discrete expectations, sequential updates, and total-derivative computation through Algorithm 1. Previously disclosed optimizers, hardware, runtime, and repository access information remain.

R1.justification: V4 adds six cited works, including Yang et al. (2024), Chen et al. (2025), Akhtiamov et al. (2024), and Liu and Ma (2024), extending application context and discussion of analytical approaches. Numerous other bibliography changes update existing works to published versions.

P1.justification: V4 makes focused explanatory and affiliation edits, changes theorem/result terminology, adds three appendix subsections, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and section ordering remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds the Algorithm 1 display and changes figure placement, notably Figures 2 and 5. All ten figure assets and the notation table retain their substantive content; the changes concern presentation rather than replacement plots.

improvement.justification: V4 improves transparency about non-rigorous theory and corrects Equation (137), but its new computational guidance contains errors: Equation (142)'s probability weights do not sum to one, and Algorithm 1's Equation (156) conflicts with Equation (149). These benefits and reproducibility problems have an uncertain net effect. The unchanged results do not establish whether the new inconsistencies are merely transcription errors or reflect the computations.
